research_question: Can satellite AI help assess developing high water when ground-monitoring data are limited?
group_weighting: equal available groups; equal available stations within peer/mainstem groups
eo_distance: L2-normalized frozen vectors; squared Euclidean/cosine distance normalized by earlier available-vector pair variance
fusion: 0.5 conventional squared distance plus 0.5 EO squared distance; no outcome-selected weights
donors: same target gauge; earlier verified 24h response complete; whole regional query storm excluded; episode closure known
historical_projection: retained query coordinates projected onto finalized historical donor input histories; earlier archive retained except explicit history-cap groups
donor_source_gaps: causal forward hold within historical input window, then earlier-archive coordinate mean if still unknown; never fill verification
maas_quality: q_strict; interpolated broader display values excluded from predictors
ground_loss_scope: local temporal thinning/gaps; all tributary observing-station subsets; Maas dropout separately identified; no full Cartesian product; two combined profiles with degraded retained feeds and no Maas inputs
rain_coarsening: completed UTC reporting blocks only; current incomplete tail uses last completed block rate; report age and inferred tail
assessment_clock: common reference rainfall landmark; controlled input-scarcity assessment, not degraded-system trigger verification
verification: original held next-24h discharge; source-quality and hindsight high-water labels retained, never input masks or ranking

uncertainty.random_masks: resample R complete timeline IDs with replacement per draw, then average; exact enumerated designs are not resampled
uncertainty.secondary: K10, timing, magnitude, coverage and width diagnostics

supporting_models.ttm: not part of the all-mask core; complete-history cached vectors are invalid under withheld inputs; any later frozen-history comparison needs its own permitted-history inference
supporting_models.alphaearth: retained supporting landscape/transfer evidence; not asserted to observe current river state

reporting.primary: recent / K5 / CRPS; equal gauge-issue cell mass
reporting.inference: exploratory paired intervals; no selected-cell winner claims
reporting.bootstrap: 999 shared whole-year block draws; globally shared mask-ID resampling of the replication mean; exact phases/subsets averaged without resampling
